description: WAHAJ is a team of students passionate about Software Engineering, AI, Data, and Space Exploration. For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we are working on Flame in Freefall, turning NASA microgravity combustion research into clear, useful insights for space fire safety. We combine software, AI/ML, data analysis, visualization, and creativity to build practical scientific solutions.
summary:
WAHAJ is an AI-powered scientific knowledge platform that transforms complex microgravity combustion research into accessible and actionable scientific insights.

Inspired by the challenge "Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data", WAHAJ helps users explore scientific investigations, retrieve relevant research findings, and understand how fire behaves in microgravity environments.

By combining NASA's scientific research with AI-assisted information retrieval and natural-language interaction, WAHAJ makes specialized combustion knowledge easier to discover and understand.

Our mission is to support scientific knowledge discovery and contribute to safer human space exploration, from future lunar habitats to missions to Mars and beyond.
details:
WAHAJ (Understanding Fire in Microgravity) is an AI-powered scientific research platform developed to make microgravity combustion research more accessible and useful for space fire-safety applications.

The Problem

Fire behaves differently in microgravity than it does on Earth. Understanding these differences is essential for protecting astronauts, spacecraft, and future lunar and Martian habitats. However, relevant scientific investigations and experimental findings are distributed across complex research documents, making them difficult to explore and interpret efficiently.

Our Solution

WAHAJ provides an integrated platform that organizes scientific combustion knowledge and enables users to explore research findings through an accessible interface.

The platform includes:

  • Scientific Dashboard: Provides an overview of the available research knowledge.
  • Research Explorer: Helps users discover and explore relevant combustion investigations and scientific sources.
  • AI Research Assistant: Allows users to ask questions in natural language and retrieve relevant information from the indexed scientific knowledge base.
  • Source-Based Responses: Connects retrieved information to its supporting research sources, helping users investigate the underlying evidence.

How It Works

The platform processes scientific research materials, organizes their content into searchable knowledge units, and uses information retrieval techniques to identify relevant evidence in response to user queries. AI-assisted synthesis helps transform retrieved information into understandable responses while maintaining connections to the original sources.

Technology Stack

  • Python for backend development and data processing.
  • FastAPI for backend API services.
  • SQLite for structured data storage and retrieval.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interactive frontend.
  • AI-assisted language processing for scientific question answering.

Our Goal and Impact

WAHAJ aims to reduce the complexity of accessing microgravity combustion research, improve scientific knowledge discovery, and support better-informed fire-safety research for future human space exploration.

Our long-term vision is to develop WAHAJ into a reliable scientific knowledge platform connecting space research with practical safety insights.
